primary_metric: Macro-F1 (guardrail: Recall of the High class)
finding_tuning: Nested grouped tuning produced no measurable gain (ΔMacro-F1 within ±0.022, far below fold std ≈0.10–0.14); hyperparameter selection itself was unstable (modal combination chosen in only 7–8/25 outer folds). Conclusion: at n=176 records / 88 groups, well-regularised defaults are as good as tuned settings; defaults are retained for deployment.
winner: Logistic Regression (default C=1.0, class_weight='balanced', standardised numerics)
rationale: Top Macro-F1: 0.608 vs XGBoost 0.601 (tuned) / 0.599 (default) — differences are within one fold-std, i.e. statistically indistinguishable.

Tie-break by documented criteria: (a) lowest variance across folds (±0.097 — most stable), (b) highest AUC 0.852, (c) best minority-class performance (Recall_Low), (d) parsimony and direct interpretability (coefficients feed the XAI layer natively), (e) fastest training/prediction.
Because the Macro-F1 gap is inside the noise band, the declaration explicitly relies on these pre-stated tie-breakers rather than claiming statistical superiority.
operational_alternative: Random Forest (defaults) achieves the highest Recall_High = 0.841 and is documented as the recommended alternative if the migration program later prioritises maximum sensitivity to High-risk cases over balanced performance.
caveats: Low class has only 15 records — its per-class figures carry wide uncertainty.
All figures are 25-fold grouped-CV means; a locked group holdout demonstration is scheduled for the defense build (Phase 5).
